reelection.rule: Rule: next even-year November for this House term. legislators-current.yaml ends the current term on 2027-01-03. The even-year November before that January 3 end is November 2026. The file has no election day, so no day of the month is shown.

vote_frequency.label: In this cached set only (the latest 40 House roll calls, not a lifetime record): 2 of 40. Yea or Aye: 1. Nay or No: 1. Not Voting: 0. Of 2 Yea or Nay votes where the Republican majority could be computed, 1 (50%) matched that majority (majority = the side most of that party's members voting Yea or Nay took; on average 217 members of that party voted Yea or Nay per roll call).

lobbying_summary.caption: From Senate lobbying disclosures (LD-2). A filing mentions this bill; it does not show what was asked for, which side the client took, or any contact with this member. Reported amounts cover the whole filing, not this bill alone.

lobbying_caption: From Senate lobbying disclosures (LD-2). A filing mentions this bill; it does not show what was asked for, which side the client took, or any contact with this member. Reported amounts cover the whole filing, not this bill alone.

donor_industry.caption: From itemized individual contributions over $200 reported to the FEC, grouped by the donor's self-reported employer and occupation. Employer means where the donor works, not that the company gave money; corporations can't give directly to campaigns. Industry groups use simple keyword rules and may misclassify some donors.
donor_industry.cycle_rule: House filings use the 2026 two-year cycle.

stands_for.caption: Grouped by Congress.gov's official policy area. Shows how they voted, not why. Final-passage, amendment, and procedural votes can mean different things; read the note for each.
stands_for.scope: House roll calls 1–323 of 2026 (323 votes, January 6, 2026 to November 12, 2026), from the House Clerk.
stands_for.majority_rule: Party majority = the Yea/Nay side taken by most members of that party who voted Yea or Nay on that roll call, counted from the party code in the roll-call XML (all members, including ones no longer serving). Ties have no majority.
stands_for.factual_flag: Not yet summarized: this line is built only from the official vote question and the bill's official title.

votes.question: On Agreeing to the Amendment (H R 8800)
votes.bill_title: National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2027
votes.plain_language: This amendment would have required the Defense Secretary to report options for cutting the department's civilian workforce by 200,000. A Yea would have added that report. A Nay voted not to add it.

votes.question: On Agreeing to the Amendment (H R 8800)
votes.bill_title: National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2027
votes.plain_language: This amendment to the fiscal year 2027 defense bill would ban automated speed-enforcement cameras on military bases. A Yea adds that ban to the bill. A Nay leaves the bill without it.

votes.question: On Agreeing to the Amendment (H R 8800)
votes.bill_title: National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2027
votes.plain_language: This amendment to H.R. 8800 (National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2027) would have let the Secretary approve any eligible investor and cleared investment professional who meets the program's requirements to assess investment opportunities matching the department's needs, with no cap on participants, according to the Congressional Research Service description. A Yea supports adopting it; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Agreeing to the Amendment (H R 8800)
votes.bill_title: National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2027
votes.plain_language: This amendment to H.R. 8800 (National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2027) is summarized by the Congressional Research Service as: “Amendment codifies protections and responsibilities for chaplains and subjects such protections to prosecution under the Uniform Code of Military Justice.” A Yea supports adding it to the bill; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Agreeing to the Amendment (H R 8800)
votes.bill_title: National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2027
votes.plain_language: This amendment to H.R. 8800 (National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2027) is summarized by the Congressional Research Service as: “Amendment sought to authorize the Secretary of Defense to establish a school choice pilot program for members of the Armed Forces.” A Yea supports adding it to the bill; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Agreeing to the Amendment (H R 8800)
votes.bill_title: National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2027
votes.plain_language: This amendment to H.R. 8800 (National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2027) is summarized by the Congressional Research Service as: “Amendment prohibits male participation in female sports at Department of Defense Education Activity schools.” A Yea supports adding it to the bill; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Agreeing to the Amendment (H R 8800)
votes.bill_title: National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2027
votes.plain_language: This amendment to H.R. 8800 (National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2027) is summarized by the Congressional Research Service as: “Amendment prohibits gender-related medical care under TRICARE and prevents TRICARE from covering certain gender-related medical procedures and treatments.” A Yea supports adding it to the bill; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Agreeing to the Amendment (H R 8800)
votes.bill_title: National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2027
votes.plain_language: This amendment to H.R. 8800 (National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2027) would have codified Executive Order 14183, which requires all personnel to serve in accordance with their biological sex, according to the Congressional Research Service description. A Yea supports adopting it; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Agreeing to the Amendment (H R 8800)
votes.bill_title: National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2027
votes.plain_language: This amendment to H.R. 8800 (National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2027) is summarized by the Congressional Research Service as: “Amendment establishes a presumption of approval for qualified Department of Defense servicemembers and civilian employees seeking authorization from their facility commander to carry personal firearms on military installations.” A Yea supports adding it to the bill; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Agreeing to the Amendment (H R 8800)
votes.bill_title: National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2027
votes.plain_language: This amendment to H.R. 8800 (National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2027) is summarized by the Congressional Research Service as: “An amendment numbered 15 printed in Part A of House Report 119-755 to prohibit funds for Ukraine Security Assistance except for U.S. embassy security in Ukraine.” A Yea supports adding it to the bill; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Agreeing to the Amendment (H R 8800)
votes.bill_title: National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2027
votes.plain_language: This amendment to H.R. 8800 (National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2027) is summarized by the Congressional Research Service as: “Amendment sought to prohibit the Department of Defense from using taxpayer funds to cover the costs of foreign military personnel participating in bilateral or multilateral military exercises conducted with the United States unless the Secretary of Defense waives the prohibition when necessary to support a U.S. national security interest.” A Yea supports adding it to the bill; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Agreeing to the Amendment (H R 8800)
votes.bill_title: National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2027
votes.plain_language: This amendment to H.R. 8800 (National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2027) is summarized by the Congressional Research Service as: “Amendment sought to preempt state and local laws that impose requirements different from federal standards on certain defense-related recycling, disposal, and materials recovery activities.” A Yea supports adding it to the bill; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Agreeing to the Amendment (H R 8800)
votes.bill_title: National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2027
votes.plain_language: This amendment to H.R. 8800 (National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2027) would have required a study of ways federal authority could preempt or otherwise mitigate state actions affecting domestic refining capacity for national defense, according to the Congressional Research Service description. A Yea supports adopting it; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Agreeing to the Amendment (H R 8800)
votes.bill_title: National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2027
votes.plain_language: This amendment to H.R. 8800 (National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2027) requires the continued operation of the Santa Ynez Pipeline System, which transports domestically produced crude oil to refineries that supply Department of Defense installations, according to the Congressional Research Service description. A Yea supports adopting it; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Agreeing to the Amendment (H R 8800)
votes.bill_title: National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2027
votes.plain_language: This amendment to H.R. 8800 (National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2027) would have barred courts from issuing injunctions that impair military readiness, military fuel supply, or defense-related logistical support, according to the Congressional Research Service description. A Yea supports adopting it; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Agreeing to the Amendment (H R 8800)
votes.bill_title: National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2027
votes.plain_language: This amendment to H.R. 8800 (National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2027) is summarized by the Congressional Research Service as: “Amendment strikes section 518, relating to the pilot program on modernization of drug testing using voice-based risk assessment technology to identify servicemembers for drug testing.” A Yea supports adding it to the bill; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Agreeing to the Amendment (H R 8800)
votes.bill_title: National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2027
votes.plain_language: This amendment to H.R. 8800 (National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2027) is summarized by the Congressional Research Service as: “Amendment sought to strike section 524, which removes the existing statutory limit on the number of cadets who may receive alternative service obligations to pursue professional athletic careers, thereby preserving the current cap.” A Yea supports adding it to the bill; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Agreeing to the Amendment (H R 8800)
votes.bill_title: National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2027
votes.plain_language: This amendment to H.R. 8800 (National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2027) is summarized by the Congressional Research Service as: “Amendment sought to strike section 521 and replace it with a prohibition on foreign nationals attending the United States Military Academies.” A Yea supports adding it to the bill; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Agreeing to the Amendment (H R 8800)
votes.bill_title: National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2027
votes.plain_language: This amendment to H.R. 8800 (National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2027) is summarized by the Congressional Research Service as: “Amendment sought to strike section 1213, relating to the deadline for the Afghanistan War Commission's final report, and maintain the current statutory reporting deadline.” A Yea supports adding it to the bill; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Agreeing to the Amendment (H R 8595)
votes.bill_title: Making appropriations for national security, Department of State, and related programs for the fiscal year ending September 30, 2027, and for other purposes.
votes.plain_language: This amendment to H.R. 8595 is summarized by the Congressional Research Service as: “An amendment numbered 20 printed in Part A of House Report 119-749 to prohibit any funds from being made available to the United Nations.” A Yea supports adding it to the bill; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Agreeing to the Amendment (H R 8595)
votes.bill_title: Making appropriations for national security, Department of State, and related programs for the fiscal year ending September 30, 2027, and for other purposes.
votes.plain_language: This amendment to H.R. 8595 is summarized by the Congressional Research Service as: “Amendment sought to prohibit funds appropriated by the Act from being used for Jordan, and accordingly reduces the National Security Investment Programs, the Foreign Military Financing Program, the Global Health Programs, and other programs accounts, collectively, by $2,100,000,000.” A Yea supports adding it to the bill; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Agreeing to the Amendment (H R 8595)
votes.bill_title: Making appropriations for national security, Department of State, and related programs for the fiscal year ending September 30, 2027, and for other purposes.
votes.plain_language: This amendment to H.R. 8595 is summarized by the Congressional Research Service as: “Amendment sought to prohibit funds appropriated by the Act from being used for Israel, and accordingly reduces the Foreign Military Financing Program account by $3,300,000,000.” A Yea supports adding it to the bill; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Agreeing to the Amendment (H R 8595)
votes.bill_title: Making appropriations for national security, Department of State, and related programs for the fiscal year ending September 30, 2027, and for other purposes.
votes.plain_language: This amendment to H.R. 8595 is summarized by the Congressional Research Service as: “Amendment sought to strike the $139,575,000 for the Global Environment Facility.” A Yea supports adding it to the bill; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Agreeing to the Amendment (H R 8595)
votes.bill_title: Making appropriations for national security, Department of State, and related programs for the fiscal year ending September 30, 2027, and for other purposes.
votes.plain_language: This amendment to H.R. 8595 is summarized by the Congressional Research Service as: “Amendment sought to eliminate funding for the Fulbright Program.” A Yea supports adding it to the bill; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Agreeing to the Amendment (H R 8469)
votes.bill_title: Making appropriations for military construction, the Department of Veterans Affairs, and related agencies for the fiscal year ending September 30, 2027, and for other purposes.
votes.plain_language: This amendment to H.R. 8469 is summarized by the Congressional Research Service as: “Amendment sought to redirect $481,832,000 from the NATO Security Investment Program account to the Military Construction, Defense-Wide account.” A Yea supports adding it to the bill; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Agreeing to the Amendment (H R 7148)
votes.bill_title: Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2026
votes.plain_language: This amendment to H.R. 7148 (Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2026) is summarized by the Congressional Research Service as: “Amendment sought to prohibit the use of funds for certain community funding projects.” A Yea supports adding it to the bill; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Agreeing to the Amendment (H R 7148)
votes.bill_title: Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2026
votes.plain_language: This amendment to H.R. 7148 (Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2026) is summarized by the Congressional Research Service as: “Amendment sought to prohibit the use of funds to implement section 24220 of the Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act, including any requirements enabling or supporting vehicle "kill switch" technology, and to prohibit federal spending for the execution or enforcement of such authorities.” A Yea supports adding it to the bill; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Agreeing to the Amendment (H R 7006)
votes.bill_title: Financial Services and General Government and National Security, Department of State, and Related Programs Appropriations Act, 2026
votes.plain_language: This amendment to H.R. 7006 is summarized by the Congressional Research Service as: “Amendment sought to eliminate funding for the National Endowment for Democracy.” A Yea supports adding it to the bill; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Agreeing to the Amendment (H R 7006)
votes.bill_title: Financial Services and General Government and National Security, Department of State, and Related Programs Appropriations Act, 2026
votes.plain_language: This amendment to H.R. 7006 is summarized by the Congressional Research Service as: “Amendment sought to reduce the District of Columbia District and Appeals Court funding by 20% and to strike the salary and expense funding for Judges Boasberg's and Judge Boardman's staffs.” A Yea supports adding it to the bill; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Agreeing to the Amendment (H R 7567)
votes.bill_title: Farm, Food, and National Security Act of 2026
votes.plain_language: This amendment to H.R. 7567 (Farm, Food, and National Security Act of 2026) is summarized by the Congressional Research Service as: “Amendment removes certain emissions standards on farm equipment.” A Yea supports adding it to the bill; a Nay opposes it.

votes.bill_title: Farm, Food, and National Security Act of 2026
votes.plain_language: This amendment to H.R. 7567 (Farm, Food, and National Security Act of 2026) is summarized by the Congressional Research Service as: “Amendment sought to add "soda" to the definition of ineligible items and defines soda as a carbonated beverage containing more than 1 gram of added sugar, artificial sweetener, or flavoring per serving.” A Yea supports adding it to the bill; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Agreeing to the Amendment, as Modified (H R 7567)
votes.bill_title: Farm, Food, and National Security Act of 2026
votes.plain_language: This amendment to H.R. 7567 (Farm, Food, and National Security Act of 2026) is summarized by the Congressional Research Service as: “Amendment revises the Agriculture Advanced Research and Development Authority program to provide federal support for sustainable agriculture and innovative sustainability solutions.” A Yea supports adding it to the bill; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Agreeing to the Amendment (H R 7567)
votes.bill_title: Farm, Food, and National Security Act of 2026
votes.plain_language: This amendment to H.R. 7567 (Farm, Food, and National Security Act of 2026) is summarized by the Congressional Research Service as: “Amendment sought to preserve greyhound racing operations in West Virginia.” A Yea supports adding it to the bill; a Nay opposes it.

votes.bill_title: Farm, Food, and National Security Act of 2026
votes.plain_language: This amendment to H.R. 7567 (Farm, Food, and National Security Act of 2026) is summarized by the Congressional Research Service as: “Amendment strikes several sections relating to pesticide labeling requirements.” A Yea supports adding it to the bill; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Agreeing to the Amendment (H R 7567)
votes.bill_title: Farm, Food, and National Security Act of 2026
votes.plain_language: This amendment to H.R. 7567 (Farm, Food, and National Security Act of 2026) is summarized by the Congressional Research Service as: “Amendment sought to repeal and prohibit future implementation of the Animal and Plant Health Inspection Service (APHIS) rule mandating electronic identification (EID) eartags for bison and cattle moving interstate.” A Yea supports adding it to the bill; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Agreeing to the Amendment (H R 7567)
votes.bill_title: Farm, Food, and National Security Act of 2026
votes.plain_language: This amendment to H.R. 7567 (Farm, Food, and National Security Act of 2026) is summarized by the Congressional Research Service as: “An amendment numbered 20 printed in Part B of House Report 119-628 to mandate a USDA report to Congress (after the SNAP restrictions pilots are completed) on implementation of the restrictions, outcomes, recommendations to Congress.” A Yea supports adding it to the bill; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Agreeing to the Amendment (H R 7567)
votes.bill_title: Farm, Food, and National Security Act of 2026
votes.plain_language: This amendment to H.R. 7567 (Farm, Food, and National Security Act of 2026) is summarized by the Congressional Research Service as: “Amendment adds hot rotisserie chicken as an eligible item to be purchased by SNAP benefits.” A Yea supports adding it to the bill; a Nay opposes it.

votes.bill_title: Farm, Food, and National Security Act of 2026

party_line.scope: House roll calls 1–323 of 2026 (323 votes, January 6, 2026 to November 12, 2026), from the House Clerk.

said_voted.caption: Posts are shown as written. A post is matched to a vote only when it names the bill number or the bill's official title. A post can mention a bill for many reasons.
said_voted.topic_caption: Recent posts grouped by simple keyword rules that are identical for every member (published at /x_topic_rules.json). A post listed under a topic is not claimed to be about any specific vote; a post can appear under more than one topic.

override.bio: Father, veteran, former senator, and now proudly representing Guam in the 119th United States Congress
override.card_note: Posts from @RepMoylan. The account listed in the public congress-legislators dataset (@JMoylanforGuam) no longer exists; this account carries X's government label and its bio names the member's office.

posts.text: It was great to meet and speak with @SecRubio at a recent @HouseForeignGOP hearing. Sec. Rubio committed to establishing a regional passport office in Guam. I look forward to working more with him as we deliver for the country and Guam! https://t.co/bYwb5qtxU4
It was great hosting Lt. Gov. Josh Tenorio in DC today to discuss the important relationship between Congress and our local government. https://t.co/MptGfehzau
This Police Week and Peace Officer Memorial Day, we remember and honor those who gave their lives and who currently serve to keep our communities safe. https://t.co/i9pORwqT8E
I am proud to co-lead this bill which will ensure our guardsmen, veterans, and service members are treated with dignity and respect. https://t.co/9DRlXDAqUE
Need help with a federal agency? Contact our district office today at (671)922-7673. https://t.co/Gxg5tG10K6
Happy Mothers’s Day to the incredible women who contribute so much to our families, communities, and society! https://t.co/auDaKSH03Q

Today is a wonderful day as we celebrate the election of Pope Leo XIV—the first American pope. I  pray for his success, guidance, and wisdom as he assumes this immense role. May God bless him and may God bless America!

Happy National Teachers Week! Educators play a significant role in shaping our island and the minds of our future generations. Thank you to all teachers for your dedication and commitment. https://t.co/4Tak8zpR6U

Today I testified in front of @HouseSmallBiz urging them to help reopen the Guam SBA office. It was a successful hearing in which my colleagues had the chance to hear about the struggles Guam and the Pacific small businesses face. https://t.co/42TYALTIB8
Thank you to Dr. Sheih for bringing this case to my attention and for looking out for the safety of Guam’s families. https://t.co/OIid3F42ed
https://t.co/sOVVG9hr5B
It’s been a busy month working to improve our island! https://t.co/epcKhqnt9e
It is important that we work to enhance US foreign policy in the Indo-Pacific, and that includes supporting economic activity in Guam. https://t.co/GMrNjaRJko

Our office has worked hard to announce new investments into our national defense capabilities in Guam. These investments made will not only strengthen our capabilities but also reaffirm our commitment to the security of our allies in the Indo-Pacific. https://t.co/Kjdqkq1ZG8

To ensure local veterans have access to quality care in Guam, I wrote to VA Secretary Doug Collin’s asking him to relocate the VA Regional office from Manila to Guam. We will never stop fighting for our veterans! https://t.co/dWr9pvaQJq

Today, the committee on Education and Workforce passed reform to federal higher education programs, which will result in over $330 billion in taxpayer savings within 10 years. These reforms to federal student aid programs will boost student success while safeguarding taxpayer funds.
Small businesses are the backbone of our economy and our office is working hard to reinstate Guam’s SBA office. https://t.co/jy0HJARJfs

Today, our district team assisted the Mangilao Mayor’s office in their TEFAP Food Commodities Distribution. Thank you to the Mayor’s office for working with us and letting us donate food rations to the community! https://t.co/hesPXt7Uyf

Congratulations to everyone who participated in the 2025 Congressional App Challenge! Yesterday I visited St. Anthony Catholic School to present them with certificates for their hard work. https://t.co/gyc7Nmg2Di

I am happy to announce the winners for the 2025 Congressional Art Competition! The first place art will be displayed at the US Capitol and the second place art will be displayed at our district office. https://t.co/mbdEZqhu3x
I met with Andersen Air Force Base leadership and toured their brand new weather radar that our office facilitated the repairs for. It’s great to see our hard work in action! https://t.co/Mha4W68s8K

We worked hard to get our bill HR 877 the “Deliver for Veterans Act” passed the finish line in the House. I continue to advocate for this bill in as it advances through the Senate. https://t.co/TGUny0hrAF

It is with a heavy heart that I join the global community in mourning the loss of His Holiness Pope Francis. His profound dedication to compassion and unity has left a lasting mark on the world. His passing represents a great loss for humanity, as his legacy of love and empathy will continue to impact generations to come.

financial_disclosures.caption: Official House financial disclosure filings from the Clerk of the House. A filing lists assets, income, liabilities, and trades the member reported; it is not proof of a conflict or of wrongdoing. Dollar ranges and asset names are in the PDF. This page links to the Clerk's copies and does not score anyone.

funding.heading: Disclosed campaign receipts
funding.detail: Federal cards show the principal campaign committee and OpenFEC totals for one two-year cycle, plus itemized Schedule A contributors. House uses 2026. Senate uses the cycle of the next election (2026, 2028, or 2030). This is not career fundraising and does not include Schedule E outside spending. Governors do not get a federal contribution list.

town_halls.note: There is no national town-hall dataset. Dates are not estimated.

disclosure_note: Disclosed contributions only; donors behind groups that do not report their own donors are not in this feed.
vote_scope: This is not a full career record. The cache is the latest 40 House rolls (2026, rolls 275-314) and 40 Senate votes (119th Congress, session 2, votes 217-256).
